title: Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major, “Eroica”
hook: The symphony Beethoven wrote for Napoleon, and then tore his name from.

painting.title: Bonaparte at the Pont d’Arcole
painting.pairingNote: Gros’s study for his portrait of the young general Bonaparte, flag in hand, painted in Milan in 1796; the hero Beethoven admired before Napoleon crowned himself emperor.

facts: Beethoven wrote the symphony mainly in 1803–04. It was first played privately in the Vienna palace of his patron, Prince Lobkowitz, in 1804, and first heard in public on 7 April 1805 at the Theater an der Wien.

He meant to name it after Napoleon Bonaparte, then First Consul of France. The story told by his pupil Ferdinand Ries goes that when Napoleon proclaimed himself emperor in May 1804, Beethoven tore the title page in half. A surviving copy of the score still shows “Bonaparte” scratched out. It was published in 1806 as *Sinfonia eroica*, “composed to celebrate the memory of a great man”, and dedicated to Lobkowitz.

Nothing this long had been written as a symphony before: the first movement alone is almost as long as a whole symphony by Haydn. Early listeners were divided, and many found it too long and too strange.
The finale is built on a tune Beethoven had already used in his ballet *The Creatures of Prometheus* (1801), about the hero who brought fire to humankind.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a heroic struggle (I), a funeral march (II), life rushing back with three horns (III), a celebration built from a bare bass line (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro con brio
movements.summary: Two hammer-blow chords, then a plain tune in the cellos. The tune is knocked off course again and again, by a wrong note, by rhythms that pull against the beat and by violent, clashing chords. The movement is the story of how it comes through. It is a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] on a scale nobody had tried before.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, in the cellos
mainIdeas.description: a simple tune that outlines the home chord, then slips onto an unexpected note and hangs there.

mainIdeas.name: The second group
mainIdeas.description: several short ideas rather than one big tune, starting with a gentle falling figure passed from instrument to instrument.

mainIdeas.name: The new theme
mainIdeas.description: a sad, singing melody in E minor that appears in the middle of the movement, far from home.

stops.hear: Two loud, short chords from the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The home key, E-flat major, stated in two blows

stops.hear: The cellos play a plain tune; after a few bars it slides onto a strange note, and the violins answer with an uneasy throbbing
stops.happening: Theme 1. The wrong note (C-sharp) is the first crack in the hero’s armour

stops.hear: A gentle falling figure is passed from oboe to clarinet to flute to violins
stops.happening: The second group of themes, in B-flat major

stops.hear: Loud, jabbing chords that seem to beat in two against the three of the bar
stops.happening: A [[hemiola|hemiola]]: the rhythm stumbles on purpose. The climax of the [[exposition|exposition]]

stops.hear: The cellos’ tune is broken into fragments and pushed into darker keys
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins

stops.hear: The instruments enter one after another on a busy figure; then a long series of hammered, grinding chords at full volume
stops.happening: A short [[fugato|fugato]], then the most violent passage in the movement

stops.hear: Out of the wreckage, the oboes sing a new, sad melody
stops.happening: A new theme, in E minor

stops.hear: Everything goes quiet; the violins tremble on a chord, and a single horn plays the cellos’ tune too early, clashing with it. A moment later the whole orchestra crashes in
stops.happening: The famous “early” horn entry, then the [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The music sets off again, as if for a second development; the E minor melody returns
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]], one of the longest Beethoven wrote

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The cellos’ tune, now in the horns and then the whole orchestra, rises again and again
stops.happening: For the first time it is heard whole, as a fanfare

notice: Follow the cellos’ tune through the movement. Almost every time it appears it is bent or interrupted, until the coda, where it finally plays out in full.
Listen for the single quiet horn just before the recapitulation. It sounds like a mistake. Ries thought so at the first rehearsal, said so, and later wrote that he was close to having his ears boxed.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Karajan recorded all nine symphonies with the Berlin Philharmonic three times for Deutsche Grammophon; this is the second cycle, made in the Philharmonie in Berlin. He does not repeat the exposition of the first movement, which is why it lasts about thirteen and a half minutes; performances that take the repeat are several minutes longer. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 1–4, followed by the *Leonore* Overture No. 3.

movements.heading: Marcia funebre: Adagio assai
movements.summary: A funeral march in C minor, slow and heavy, with a shuddering figure in the basses like muffled drums. A short, consoling middle section in C major gives way to a [[fugue|fugue]] and an outburst of grief. At the end the march tune falls apart into fragments separated by silence.

mainIdeas.name: The march
mainIdeas.description: a low, sombre tune in the violins over a growling figure in the basses.

mainIdeas.name: The second tune
mainIdeas.description: a gentler phrase in the major that soon sinks back into the minor.

mainIdeas.name: The major section
mainIdeas.description: a brighter melody for oboe, flute and bassoon over flowing strings.

stops.hear: Very quiet: the violins play a slow, low march tune; the basses answer with a short, shuddering growl
stops.happening: The march theme, in C minor. The bass figure imitates muffled drums

stops.hear: The oboe takes the tune, plaintive and alone
stops.happening: The march repeated in a new colour

stops.hear: A gentler, rising phrase in the major, which soon darkens again
stops.happening: The second theme, in E-flat major

stops.hear: The mood lifts: oboe, flute and bassoon sing over flowing strings, then the full orchestra with trumpets and drums rings out
stops.happening: The major section, in C major (Beethoven marks it *Maggiore*). Consolation, then a glimpse of glory

stops.hear: The march returns, but after a few bars it changes course: the instruments enter one after another, weaving a dense web
stops.happening: A [[fugue|fugue]], in F minor. The march becomes a lament of many voices

stops.hear: A crushing outburst with the full brass, then a stark, hollow passage
stops.happening: The emotional peak of the movement

stops.hear: The march tune returns in the oboe, in the home key
stops.happening: The opening comes back

stops.hear: A quiet marching figure from the major section, then a last, slow approach to the tune
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: The tune comes back one last time and breaks into short phrases with silences between them
stops.happening: The march crumbles and ends very quietly

notice: Listen to the basses in the first minute. Their short growl after each phrase sounds like a drum roll in a real funeral procession.
In the last bars the tune is broken into pieces with silence between them, as if the mourners can no longer speak.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: After the funeral, life rushes back. Quiet, fast and nervous at first, the [[scherzo|scherzo]] gathers until the whole orchestra bursts out. The middle section, the [[trio|trio]], belongs to three horns, one more than symphonies of the time normally used.

mainIdeas.name: The scherzo
mainIdeas.description: quick, whispered short notes in the strings, with a little tune in the oboe.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a ringing fanfare for three horns, like a hunting call.

stops.hear: The strings whisper fast, short notes; an oboe picks out a little tune
stops.happening: The scherzo begins very quietly, as if from a distance, and not yet in the home key

stops.hear: Suddenly the whole orchestra bursts in, loud
stops.happening: The tune arrives in the home key, E-flat major

stops.hear: Three horns play a ringing fanfare; strings and woodwinds answer softly
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]]. The third horn was the novelty

stops.hear: The fast, whispering strings return
stops.happening: The scherzo again

stops.hear: A loud descending figure in [[unison|unison]] suddenly lurches into a different rhythm, in two instead of three
stops.happening: Beethoven changes the metre for four bars

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A quick build from very soft to very loud, and a sharp ending
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: In the trio, listen for the three horns playing together in close harmony. In Beethoven’s day these were natural horns without valves, the instrument of the hunt.

movements.heading: Finale: Allegro molto
movements.summary: A set of [[variation|variation]]s that starts from almost nothing. After a rushing opening, Beethoven presents only the bass line of his theme, plucked and bare. He builds on it layer by layer before the real melody appears, and then takes it through two fugues, a dance, a slow hymn and a final dash.

mainIdeas.name: The bass
mainIdeas.description: a skeleton of a tune, plucked by the strings, with long pauses.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a cheerful, simple tune first heard in the oboe; it comes from Beethoven’s *Prometheus* ballet.

stops.hear: A rush of strings, then loud chords
stops.happening: The introduction

stops.hear: The strings pluck a bare, halting line, with silences between the notes
stops.happening: The bass line of the theme, on its own, in [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]

stops.hear: The same bass line, now bowed, with new lines woven around it
stops.happening: The first [[variation|variation]]s: the theme is being built up

stops.hear: A cheerful, simple tune appears in the oboe, on top of the bass line
stops.happening: The real melody, from the *Prometheus* ballet

stops.hear: The strings enter one after another on a quiet, busy subject, building tension
stops.happening: A [[fugue|fugue]] on the bass line

stops.hear: Bright and light; a flute flutters above the tune
stops.happening: A variation in D major

stops.hear: Fierce and stamping, in the minor
stops.happening: A wild, dance-like variation in G minor

stops.hear: Another fugue, this time bright and in the home key, building to a big climax
stops.happening: The second fugue

stops.hear: Everything slows down; the oboe sings the melody as a tender, hymn-like song
stops.happening: *Poco andante*: the theme turned into a hymn

stops.hear: The horns blaze the melody out over the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The heroic climax of the symphony

stops.label: Last 45 seconds
stops.hear: A sudden, very fast dash and three huge chords
stops.happening: The *Presto* [[coda|coda]]

notice: The finale begins with only the bass of the theme. Notice how long Beethoven makes you wait for the melody, and how familiar it seems when it arrives.

threads.title: A hero’s story
threads.body: Struggle (I), death (II), life returning (III), celebration (IV). This reading is old, and Beethoven’s title, “to celebrate the memory of a great man”, invites it.

threads.title: The tune that came first
threads.body: The finale’s theme existed before the symphony. Some scholars hear its outline already in the cellos’ tune of the first movement, so that the whole symphony grows towards it.

threads.title: Horns
threads.body: The early horn entry in the first movement, the three horns of the trio and the horns’ blaze in the finale: the hunting instrument becomes the voice of the hero.
